title: Introduce compact econ templates & latency-aware sampling profiler
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: We routinely see customers with crisp latency SLOs overpaying for capacity because default batching and quantization settings are conservative. This PR introduces a compact "econ template" family: lightweight, validated combinations of batching hints, KV cache aggressiveness, and quantization presets that prioritize unit cost reduction while keeping P95 latency within customer SLO targets. Complementing templates is a latency-aware sampling profiler (LASP) that runs short, low-overhead traffic samplers to infer sequence length distributions and tail behavior, and then recommends one of the compact templates or a conservative fallback.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a library of compact econ templates (small, medium, conservative) encoded as JSON templates plus an evaluation harness for offline simulation. Templates encode: batch target, max_wait_ms, kv_cache_mode, quant_profile (int8/int4 where available), and safe-fallback heuristics.
- Implements LASP (latency-aware sampling profiler): a background service that can run for a configurable window per model/route, collects sampled inference traces with anonymized token-length histograms and P95 latency estimates, and scores templates against cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Introduces a suggestion API endpoint (/v1/optimize/suggest-template) that returns a ranked list of templates, expected unit-cost delta, and a conservative-score. The endpoint is gated behind role-based access and opt-in telemetry.
- Adds a console panel with a compact-templates UI (docs and screenshots included) exposing suggested changes and a one-click apply for Dedicated/Hosted customers.
- Unit and integration tests for sampler heuristics, template scoring, and safe-fallback behavior. Performance microbenchmarks included; we mark the perf tests as flaky on some ARM runners and guard them in CI.

Why this is different from prior work: Existing autotuners in the repo focus on aggressive prefill or probabilistic batch allocation. This change targets small, easily-auditable templates intended for quick adoption by product teams and for the Console to show actionable suggestions. LASP is intentionally low-intrusion: it only samples up to a configurable qps and uses k-anonymized histograms so it is safe for private deployments.

Checklist:
- [x] Templates schema and JSON examples
- [x] LASP sampler implementation + config knobs
- [x] Suggestion API + request/response contract docs
- [x] Console UI wiring and help text
- [x] Tests (unit + integration)
- [x] Docs: docs/opt/compact-templates.md
- [x] Linear tickets updated (ENG-4821, ENG-5013)

Backwards compatibility and safety: Applying a template by default does not auto-upgrade live routes. The suggested template flow in the Console applies changes to a staging config which can be validated against existing latency telemetry and run as a canary. For Private installs the sampler is disabled by default and requires admin opt-in.

Notes on evaluation: LASP scoring uses a simulated batching-cost estimator (existing cost model) plus empirical P95 from samples. We add an upper confidence bound for latency; templates that exceed the chosen confidence threshold are marked as conservative and are recommended only when cost wins are small.

Related: This interacts with autoscaling policies; default scale thresholds are honored and template application will not lower autoscaler capacity. See docs/opt/compact-templates.md for the full decision matrix.
